as_of_note: Sourced CONTEXT, never a scoring input. Compiled 2026-10-30 by the Canada source-audit lane. StatCan figures read through the Web Data Service on 2026-10-30 (monthly tables through 2026-08; annual figures are full calendar years); values marked 'Derived' are arithmetic on the cited series, done in this audit. CER profile figures carry their data year, not the page's modification date. Omitted for lack of a readable official figure: world rank as an energy producer (the NRCan Energy Fact Book could not be fetched: TLS certificate chain error).

metrics.source: Statistics Canada, Table 25-10-0029-01, Primary energy / Production (vector v54272546)
metrics.note: Primary energy as StatCan defines it: crude oil, natural gas, gas-plant NGLs, coal, primary electricity (hydro and nuclear), steam, renewable fuels. Uranium is not counted as a fuel. 24,664 PJ.
metrics.basis: country total, calendar year; primary energy production as Statistics Canada defines it

metrics.source: Statistics Canada, Table 25-10-0063-01, Crude oil production, Canada, barrels (vector v107757045)
metrics.note: Derived: 1,748,642,834 bbl summed over the 12 months of 2025, divided by 365. Excludes condensate and pentanes plus (reported separately as equivalent products).
metrics.basis: country total, calendar-year average derived from monthly sums; crude oil including bitumen and synthetic crude, excluding condensate and pentanes plus

metrics.source: Statistics Canada, Table 25-10-0063-01 (vectors v107757053, v107757061, v107757045)
metrics.note: Derived: (non-upgraded crude bitumen 799,213,544 + synthetic crude oil 477,946,221) / crude oil production 1,748,642,834 bbl. Table identity checked: crude production = net field production + synthetic; net field = heavy + light/medium + non-upgraded bitumen.
metrics.basis: share of the crude oil production total above, same table and year

metrics.basis: country total, calendar year; LNG exports, natural-gas-equivalent volume, all terminals

significance: In 2025 Canada produced about 4.8 million barrels per day of crude oil, about 73% of it oil-sands bitumen or upgraded synthetic crude, and about 85% of it in Alberta.
Hydro supplied about 55% of Canada's 625 TWh of electricity generated in 2025.
Canada began large-scale LNG exports from Kitimat, British Columbia, in June 2025.
Alberta ended coal-fired generation by June 2024, and federal regulations end the useful life of coal-fired units no later than 31 December 2029.
